Walk a measured distance (a running track straight is exactly 100 m; a 25-m pool is 25 m). The step counter divides into your distance to derive a personal stride length.

Strap Bluetooth bike speed sensors (CSC) to wheel hubs — they become rally wheel probes. Two on the same axle measure the exact vehicle centreline; mount on a non-driven axle.
Bluetooth permissions are required to scan for sensors.

Race a virtual partner. Pick an even pace, a goal time over a distance, or a past run — then start recording on the Runner dashboard.

Write the GPS chip\'s raw NMEA sentences to cache/nmea/ during recordings. Off by default; for debugging chip behaviour.
Rebroadcast raw NMEA sentences over Bluetooth Serial Port (RFCOMM) during recordings, so a paired chart-plotter or desktop tool can use the phone as an external GPS puck.

Everything below works offline — no Play Services, no API keys, no telemetry. Quick tour:
Live position, satellites, compass, speed, sun. Tap any card to open its detail screen.
Tap the red dot at the bottom-right to start. Recording continues in the background.
Tap the pin icon in the top bar to save the current fix as a one-point trail.
The map icon in the top bar opens the trails list — import GPX, share, and view on an offline-capable map.
If the app has been useful, a 5-star rating on the Play Store helps other people find it. It only takes a moment.
Version %1$s is on the Play Store — tap to update.
Wave the phone in a figure-8 motion to recalibrate the magnetometer.
Download OSM tiles for this trail\'s bounding box so the map renders without a network later.
Shown while a GPS trail is being recorded in the background.
GPS capture continues while the app is open or pocketed. Tap to return.
Dots: recent readings. Ring: estimated hard-iron offset.\nA well-calibrated phone draws a tight ring centred on the cross.
Within the expected Earth-field range (22 – 70 µT).
Outside the expected Earth-field range. Move away from metal, magnets, speakers and laptops, then try again.

1. Move away from large metal objects, magnets, speakers and laptops.
2. Hold the phone in your hand and slowly rotate it through every orientation — a figure-of-eight motion works.
3. Keep going until the accuracy chip reads HIGH and coverage approaches 100 %%.

The phone never stops calibrating in the background; this screen just gives you a way to see what it has measured.
Sky view. %1$d satellites in view, %2$d used in fix, average signal %3$.1f decibels.
Gimballed compass. Heading %1$03d degrees magnetic, %2$s. Pitch %3$+.0f degrees, roll %4$+.0f degrees.
Magnetometer %1$s projection. Estimated hard-iron offset %2$+.1f, %3$+.1f microtesla.
Set a target pace for the segment leading to each waypoint. The Sports view will follow these per-segment targets instead of the overall one.
Tap the map to place your destination, then confirm.
Enter a latitude in [-90, 90] and a longitude in [-180, 180].
Enter the pace you want to hold. Live deviation will appear on the navigation card and audible cues will fire on threshold cross.
Tap a device to pair. Only Bluetooth heart-rate monitors using the standard Heart Rate Service are supported.
Looking for monitors… make sure your strap is awake and nearby.
Bluetooth permissions are required to pair a monitor.
Tap a device to pair. Only Bluetooth power meters using the standard Cycling Power Service are supported.
Looking for power meters… spin the crank or wake the meter and keep it nearby.
Bluetooth permissions are required to pair a power meter.
Have a friend scan this QR with their camera or QR app — it opens their default maps app pinned to your current spot.
Waiting for a GPS fix to share…
QR code containing the geo URI for the current position
Waiting for a GPS fix before capturing a waypoint…
No waypoints yet. Tap the + button below to drop one at your current spot.
Filter raw GPS altitude through a low-pass to suppress per-sample jitter. The readout still tracks real climbs but stops bouncing on a level walk.
Set your maximum HR and tune the zone boundaries. The defaults follow the standard 60/70/80/90 % breakdown; trained athletes typically push Z3–Z5 higher.
No monitor paired. Pair one in Settings.
Spoken pace and zone feedback during the Sports view. Uses the device\'s on-board text-to-speech — no network required.
What do you want to do?
GPSinfo is now organised by what you want to do. Pick an activity to dive in; your full dashboard lives under Custom / Everything.
Get there — address search, route, live map.
Search for an address or place and follow an offline turn-by-turn route on a live vector map, with your speed at a glance. Tap to open the map, then search or pick a saved place.
Record a run or ride and pace yourself.
Record a GPX/FIT trail with distance, time and pace; add a ghost runner, pace targets and heart-rate or power sensors. Start recording from the dashboard and review trails afterwards.
Where am I, where\'s that, mark this.
A precise compass, your coordinates in any format, waypoints to mark and share spots, plus sun/moon and a world view. Open the compass, then reach waypoints and sharing from there.
See the raw signal — satellites, NMEA, fix quality.
Inspect the sky plot, per-satellite signal strength, fix status and accuracy, and the raw NMEA stream. For the curious, for surveying, and for diagnosing reception.
Hold an exact average over a stage.
Run a regularity stage to a target average speed with a live early/late delta, wheel-sensor distance and ±recalibration. Arm the stage, then start on the marshal\'s go.
Your full, editable dashboard — all cards on one screen.
The classic all-in-one dashboard: pick exactly which cards show and in what order. Everything the app can do, on a single screen, the way you arrange it.
